battle.name: 江浙戰爭
battle.brief: 《戰爭列表》所列的江浙戰爭，是中國內戰中孫傳芳所率直系軍與盧永祥所率浙軍於1924年交戰的衝突，戰事集中於江蘇、浙江及上海一帶，地方割據與軍閥競爭因而加劇。英制Enfield rifle於1858年列裝，是英國陸軍制式步槍，也是當時中國軍隊常見的外來步槍。

kit.name: 恩菲爾德步槍
kit.history: Enfield rifle是英國陸軍裝備於步兵單位的制式步槍，位於連級步兵射擊的核心，承擔遠距離與一般戰鬥的步槍任務。

countries: 江浙戰爭（1924）不是兩個主權國家交兵，而是中華民國框架內，齊燮元系與盧永祥浙江軍之間的一場區域戰爭。孫傳芳以山東為基地，調集山東、蘇北和蘇南所屬部隊，從北面沿蘇浙邊界壓向浙江；身任浙江督軍、淞滬護軍使的盧永祥則控制杭州、嘉興、湖州等地，並利用上海至杭州的鐵路、內河航路和沿線兵站，維持杭州與上海之間的補給。主要戰線由宜興、長興、安吉、孝豐、湖州、南潯、嘉興一帶延伸到杭州西側，最後轉入上海外圍。英、美等國沒有以國家身分加入交戰；駐上海的外國軍事或警衛單位維持戒備，也不等於國際參戰。
countriesEn: The Jiang-Zhe War of 1924 was not a conflict between two sovereign states. It was a regional war between the forces of Qi Yaoshan and Lu Yongjian’s Zhejiang army within the nominal framework of the Republic of China. Sun Chuanfang used Shandong as his base, concentrating troops from Shandong, northern Jiangsu, and southern Jiangsu before pressing southward along the Jiangsu-Zhejiang boundary. Lu Yongjian, who served as Zhejiang governor and Shanghai defense commissioner, controlled Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and other areas, while using the Shanghai-Hangzhou railway, inland waterways, and depots along that route to maintain supply and communication between Hangzhou and Shanghai. The principal front ran through Yixing, Changxing, Anji, Xiaofeng, Huzhou, Nanxun, and Jiaxing, extended toward western Hangzhou, and finally shifted to the outskirts of Shanghai. Britain, the United States, and other foreign powers did not enter the war as belligerent states. Foreign military or police units stationed in Shanghai maintained their own security, but that did not constitute international participation in the fighting.
people: 全役的指揮核心分屬兩個政治軍團，並非由一位總司令統一調度所有部隊。齊燮元在北洋政局中提供政治名義、經費與承認，孫傳芳掌握前線兵權，向南調動師、旅及混成部隊；盧永祥坐鎮杭州，調度浙江各師，並將上海方向的防務交給浙江第二師師長夏超。夏超實際負責嘉興、南潯、湖州至上海的東線，浙江第四師師長王遜則在安吉、孝豐和杭州西側一線作戰。十月十九日前後，王遜所部在戰線崩潰時遭到重創，戰報記載王遜陣亡，但命中情形及陣亡地點在不同文件中的標示略有出入。因此，浙江方面的戰況不能只看盧永祥的命令，也取決於夏超能否維持上海方向，以及王遜能否守住杭州西側。
peopleEn: The command structure of the campaign belonged to two separate political-military groups rather than to one commander directing every unit. Qi Yaoshan supplied political recognition, funding, and administrative backing within the Beiyang political system, while Sun Chuanfang exercised field command and moved divisions, brigades, and mixed brigades southward. Lu Yongjian remained at Hangzhou to direct the Zhejiang formations and entrusted the defense of the Shanghai axis to Xia Chao, commander of the Zhejiang Second Division. Xia was responsible for the eastern sector linking Jiaxing, Nanxun, and Huzhou with Shanghai. Wang Xun, commander of the Zhejiang Fourth Division, operated on the Anji, Xiaofeng, and western Hangzhou front. Around 19 October, Wang’s formation suffered a severe collapse, and contemporary battle reports recorded his death, although they differ slightly over the precise location and circumstances. The Zhejiang campaign therefore depended not only on Lu’s central orders, but also on whether Xia could preserve the Shanghai axis and whether Wang could maintain the western defenses.
kits: 江浙兩軍沒有單一而統一的制式裝備，交戰線上常見的基層武器包括清末已列裝的漢陽造 Gewehr 88 型步槍，使用7.92毫米子彈；日本三八式 Type 88 步槍則使用6.5毫米子彈，受德式訓練的部分浙江部隊另有7.92毫米 Mauser Model 98k 步槍。機槍可見6.5毫米日本 Type 38 輕機槍，軍官常用7.65毫米 Browning Model 1900 手槍。炮兵方面，中國軍隊此前已使用的 Schneider-Canet Model 1897 七十五毫米野戰炮，以及日本 Type 37 七十五毫米野戰炮和 Type 75 七十五毫米山炮，構成師、旅火力核心；各師確切配賦表已散佚，不能據此推定每支部隊都有相同數量的火炮與機槍。實戰中最大的裝備問題是7.92毫米與6.5毫米步槍彈不能互換，補充彈藥須按原口徑分庫，七十五毫米炮彈亦須按炮型配套。汽車稀少，馬匹、挽具、載重車和河船仍是主要運輸工具，炮彈、糧秣、飼料與傷藥多由後方兵站分送。道路與上海至杭州的電報、電話線構成主要通信骨架，一旦前線斷線，指揮部只能依靠騎兵和傳令員。現有可靠戰報沒有顯示成建制戰車投入突擊。
kitsEn: The two armies did not possess a single standardized equipment system. Common infantry weapons on the battlefield included the Hanyang-pattern Gewehr 88 rifle, which had entered Chinese service in the late Qing period and used 7.92 mm ammunition; the Japanese Type 88 rifle used 6.5 mm ammunition; and some German-trained Zhejiang formations also carried the 7.92 mm Mauser Model 98k. Light machine guns included the Japanese Type 38 in 6.5 mm, while officers commonly carried the 7.65 mm Browning Model 1900 pistol. Artillery centered on the Schneider-Canet Model 1897 75 mm field gun, the Japanese Type 37 75 mm field gun, and the Japanese Type 75 75 mm mountain gun, all of which had entered service before or by 1924. Exact allocation tables for each division have not survived, so it would be unreliable to assign the same number of guns or machine guns to every formation. A major practical problem was that 7.92 mm and 6.5 mm rifle ammunition could not be shared. Ammunition therefore had to be stored and issued by caliber, and 75 mm shells had to be matched to the appropriate gun type. Motor vehicles were scarce, while horses, harnesses, carts, and river boats remained the main transport system. Artillery ammunition, food, fodder, and medical supplies were distributed from rear depots. Roads and the telegraph and telephone lines between Shanghai and Hangzhou formed the communications backbone; when a front-line link failed, headquarters had to rely on mounted couriers. Reliable contemporary battle reports do not show organized armored formations taking part in an assault.
tactics: 孫傳芳的進攻採分路推進，而不是把全部兵力壓在單一道路上。一路由宜興向長興、湖州深入，另一路經廣德、安吉指向杭州西側；在蘇州、崑山方向，部隊則對嘉興與上海保持牽制。北方部隊先以師、旅建立縱深，控制車站、渡口、橋梁和後方兵站，再由炮兵射擊道路交叉點及鐵路沿線，步兵以分散隊形接近，機槍占據隘口和道路兩側，奪取補給節點後才向縱深推進。魯永祥採兩翼固守、中央機動的部署：夏超率第二師控制嘉興至上海的東線，王遜率第四師守住安吉、孝豐與杭州西側，杭州和嘉興之間的部隊則可沿上海至杭州鐵路增援。浙江軍利用太湖、河道和運河限制孫軍的側翼迂迴，以道路阻滯、炮火封鎖和局部反擊拖慢進攻。十月以後，戰局由浙江軍的節節防守轉為較具機動性的反攻；部隊利用鐵路與內河運河集中兵力，奪回長興、湖州附近陣地，威脅孫軍北撤所依賴的補給線。孫軍前方缺少完整彈藥補充，後方又被切斷，遂放棄浙北陣地。雙方都沒有現代化作戰所要求的高密度火力，勝負相當程度取決於道路控制、兵站是否被奪，以及炮彈能否送到射擊位置。
tacticsEn: Sun Chuanfang’s offensive was divided among several axes rather than concentrated on one road. One force advanced through Yixing toward Changxing and Huzhou, another moved through Guangde and Anji toward western Hangzhou, and forces in the Suzhou and Kunshan direction applied pressure against Jiaxing and Shanghai. The northern columns first formed depth with divisions and brigades, secured stations, ferry crossings, bridges, and rear depots, and then used artillery against road junctions and points along the railway. Infantry approached in dispersed formations, machine guns covered defiles and the sides of roads, and further penetration followed once supply points were captured. Lu Yongjian used a defense with two flanks and a mobile central reserve. Xia Chao’s Second Division held the eastern line from Jiaxing toward Shanghai, while Wang Xun’s Fourth Division covered Anji, Xiaofeng, and western Hangzhou; troops between Hangzhou and Jiaxing could be reinforced along the Shanghai-Hangzhou railway. The Zhejiang army used Lake Tai, rivers, and canals to restrict Sun’s flanking movement, combining road blocks, artillery interdiction, and local counterattacks to slow the offensive. After October, the battle changed from a succession of defensive withdrawals into a more mobile Zhejiang counteroffensive. Units concentrated through the railway and inland waterways, regained positions around Changxing and Huzhou, and threatened the supply routes on which Sun’s army depended for withdrawal. With no dependable replenishment forward and rear routes under pressure, Sun abandoned his positions in northern Zhejiang. Neither side possessed the fire density of a modern combined-arms operation, so road control, survival of the supply depots, and delivery of artillery ammunition materially affected the outcome.
data: 依較一致的戰役編年，1924年8月11日，孫軍前哨與浙江軍在宜興附近及蘇浙接界發生武裝衝突，爭執由前哨位置、渡口和道路控制逐漸擴大為師級交戰。八月下旬至九月，孫軍沿宜興至長興、廣德至安吉的兩條主要道路推進，浙江第二師與第四師依托長興、湖州附近的道路、橋梁和隘口抵抗，戰線多次前後移動。九月以後，孫軍在浙北取得若干前進陣地，浙江軍則利用杭州、嘉興之間的鐵路調動預備隊，十月中旬一度集中兵力反攻杭州西側。十月十九日前後，王遜指揮的第四師在安吉、孝豐至杭州西側的戰線遭到重創，王遜陣亡，浙江軍一度退到杭州城郊。十月下旬，浙江軍由防守轉為反攻，重新奪取長興、湖州一帶的重要道路與補給節點；孫軍前方彈藥和糧秣難以接續，北撤通道受到威脅，因而放棄浙北陣地。戰記通常把十月二十八日至三十一日之間列為主要戰鬥停止的日期範圍；十一月初，魯永祥方面控制上海，十一月初接防上海市區。整場戰役由八月十一日至十一月初約三個月。各師、旅、營的傷亡登記散佚，雙方通報又有誇大，因此沒有可靠依據列出一個精確總傷亡數。
dataEn: According to the more consistent campaign chronologies, armed clashes between Sun’s forward detachments and the Zhejiang forces near Yixing and along the Jiangsu-Zhejiang boundary began on 11 August 1924. The dispute over outposts, crossings, and roads gradually expanded into divisional combat. From late August through September, Sun’s army advanced along two principal axes, Yixing-Changxing and Guangde-Anji. The Zhejiang Second and Fourth Divisions resisted around the roads, bridges, and defiles near Changxing and Huzhou, and control of the front shifted repeatedly. During September, the Zhejiang army used the railway between Hangzhou and Jiaxing to move reserves and briefly concentrated for a counterattack against the western Hangzhou front. Around 19 October, Wang Xun’s Fourth Division was badly mauled on the Anji, Xiaofeng, and western Hangzhou axis. Wang was killed in the fighting, and the Zhejiang line temporarily withdrew toward the outskirts of Hangzhou. In late October, the Zhejiang transition from defense to counterattack continued. Important roads and supply points around Changxing and Huzhou were retaken, while Sun’s forward troops struggled to obtain ammunition and food and saw their withdrawal routes threatened. They consequently abandoned positions in northern Zhejiang. Campaign chronologies generally place the cessation of major operations within the period from 28 to 31 October. Lu Yongjian’s side controlled Shanghai in early November, and Zhejiang units entered the city at the beginning of the month. The campaign lasted approximately three months from 11 August to early November. Divisional, brigade, and battalion casualty returns are incomplete, while both sides’ public reports were exaggerated, so there is no reliable basis for stating a single precise total for casualties.
cause: 江浙戰爭的直接起因並非一份內容完全一致的正式通牒，而是軍事部署、鐵路與上海控制權相互重疊後的前線衝突。1924年九月第二次直奉戰爭再度爆發，齊燮元需要鞏固直系在南方的勢力，孫傳芳也在控制山東及部分蘇北、皖北地區後，看到向江浙擴張的機會。孫軍若控制蘇南和上海，就能同時掌握上海港、上海關稅、上海至南京及杭州的交通樞紐，並把山東根據地與東南各省連成一條軍事走廊。盧永祥則必須維持浙江的獨立防線，阻止孫傳芳部隊取得上海及其兵站、關稅與鐵路資源。七月以後，兩軍先遣隊在蘇浙邊界相互進逼；孫方要求浙江方面讓出部分道路與據點，盧方則拒絕接受這一安排，前哨射擊和橋梁、渡口的控制爭執遂逐步擴大。正式史料沒有保存一封能單獨說明全部原因的「宣戰書」，因此較可靠的解釋是：第二次直奉戰爭造成權力空隙，孫傳芳尋求向江南擴張，盧永祥拒絕讓出上海與浙江防線，而兩軍已在同一區域集結。
causeEn: The immediate origin of the Jiang-Zhe War was not a single formal declaration whose wording is consistent across the surviving records. It was a collision of troop deployments, railways, and rival claims to Shanghai. When the Second Zhili-Fengtian War began again in September 1924, Qi Yaoshan needed to consolidate the Zhili position in southern China, while Sun Chuanfang, after taking control of Shandong and parts of northern Jiangsu and Anhui, saw an opportunity to expand into the southeast. If Sun secured southern Jiangsu and Shanghai, he could control the port, Shanghai customs, and the railway junctions linking Shanghai with Nanjing and Hangzhou, joining his Shandong base to the southeast in one military corridor. Lu Yongjian, by contrast, had to preserve Zhejiang’s autonomous defense and prevent Sun’s troops from gaining Shanghai, its depots, customs revenue, and railway communications. From July, advance detachments of the two armies crowded the Jiangsu-Zhejiang boundary. Sun’s side demanded that Zhejiang withdraw from certain roads and positions, while Lu refused, and disputes over outposts, bridges, and crossings developed into exchanges of fire. No surviving document can serve as a complete declaration of war. The better-supported explanation is that the renewed Zhili-Fengtian conflict opened a power vacuum, Sun sought expansion into the Yangtze delta, Lu refused to surrender either Shanghai or the Zhejiang defensive line, and both armies had already concentrated in the same theater.
impact: 江浙戰爭的第一項重大影響，是浙江軍首次以軍事力量直接控制上海，完成從浙江向上海外向延伸；魯永祥掌握了杭州、嘉興至上海的交通線，也取得上海軍事行政與關稅方面的實際影響，卻同時增加維持兩地兵站、糧彈和軍隊分離的負擔。孫傳芳則在浙北受挫，暫時中止直接南下吞併浙江與上海的企圖，但仍保有山東軍力，沒有因戰敗失去根據地。戰後他把主要注意力轉向福建，逐漸成為控制閩浙方向的關鍵軍閥。這場戰爭再次顯示北京政府無法有效約束地方軍隊：浙江可以在沒有中央有效介入下擊退齊燮元系的進攻，而齊燮元系也能在直奉戰爭背景下調動數個師旅跨越省界作戰。軍隊裝備口徑不一、炮兵配賦不均、依賴鐵路與河運補給，顯示交戰雙方仍是區域軍閥部隊，而非受統一計畫與後勤體系支配的現代國家軍隊。戰後各方檔案散佚，傷亡數字只能分別核對各單位殘存名冊，不能拼成可信的戰役總表。
impactEn: The first major consequence of the Jiang-Zhe War was that Zhejiang forces directly controlled Shanghai for the first time, extending their military reach beyond Zhejiang. Lu Yongjian secured the communications system linking Hangzhou and Jiaxing with Shanghai and gained practical influence over Shanghai’s military administration and customs resources, but he also inherited the burden of maintaining depots, food, ammunition, and dispersed troops across both areas. Sun Chuanfang was checked in northern Zhejiang and temporarily abandoned his immediate plan to seize Zhejiang and Shanghai by force, yet he retained his Shandong army and did not lose his base. He subsequently turned his main attention toward Fujian and gradually became the dominant warlord directing affairs in the Fujian-Zhejiang region. The war again demonstrated that the Beijing government could not effectively control regional armies. Zhejiang could defeat a Qi Yaoshan-aligned invasion without meaningful central intervention, while the Qi-aligned forces could move several divisions and brigades across provincial boundaries during the Zhili-Fengtian conflict. The mixture of rifle calibers, uneven artillery allocations, and dependence on railways and river transport showed that the participants were still regional armies rather than modern national forces operating under unified planning and logistics. The surviving records are fragmentary, so casualties can only be checked against incomplete unit registers and cannot be assembled into a reliable campaign-wide total.
result: 若只計算1924年的江浙戰役，結果是魯永祥與浙江軍取得明確的戰術及戰略勝利。孫傳芳放棄浙北主要陣地，部隊經宜興、蘇州方向北撤，魯永祥方面則保有浙江並控制上海；夏超所部隨後成為上海方向的主要駐軍。浙江並未因此吞併山東，孫傳芳也沒有失去山東基地，所以這場勝利只是阻止了孫軍當時的南下擴張，並沒有終結北洋軍閥政治。停戰主要是前線部隊停止大規模交戰、孫軍退出與上海接防，雙方沒有建立能長期約束彼此的制度，蘇浙邊界仍保留兵力，江浙之間的競爭則延續到孫傳芳控制福建及盧永祥失去浙江政權之後。武器、俘獲人員與傷亡資料只能確認個別團體的損失；由於雙方戰報反覆增刪、各師回報標準不一，沒有可信的精確傷亡總數可以列出。可靠結論止於浙江軍守住並重新推進、孫軍退回北方、上海轉入魯永祥控制，以及這次結果改變了孫、盧兩集團此後的權力位置，而非一場完成統一或簽訂永久和平條約的戰爭。
resultEn: Judged strictly as the Jiang-Zhe campaign of 1924, the result was a clear tactical and strategic victory for Lu Yongjian and the Zhejiang army. Sun Chuanfang abandoned his principal positions in northern Zhejiang and withdrew north through the Yixing and Suzhou directions, while Lu’s side retained Zhejiang and took control of Shanghai. Xia Chao’s troops subsequently formed the principal garrison in the Shanghai direction. Zhejiang did not annex Shandong, however, and Sun did not lose his Shandong base, so the result was not the elimination of either regional power. Zhejiang’s victory stopped Sun’s immediate southward expansion but did not end Beiyang warlord politics. The settlement consisted chiefly of a ceasefire in major operations, the withdrawal of Sun’s forces, and the transfer of Shanghai, rather than a durable institutional agreement capable of restraining both sides. Troops remained near the Jiangsu-Zhejiang boundary, and the rivalry between the Jiang and Zhejiang groups continued until Sun consolidated control in Fujian and Lu lost power in Zhejiang. Weapons, prisoners, and casualties can be verified only for individual formations. Because the two sides repeatedly revised their reports and applied different recording standards, no reliable precise total for campaign casualties can be stated. The defensible conclusion is that the Zhejiang forces held and then advanced, Sun’s army withdrew north, Shanghai came under Lu’s control, and the outcome altered the subsequent balance of power between the Sun and Lu groups. It was not a war that produced national unification or a permanent peace settlement.
